tip: After когда (kagda = when) about the future, Russian uses the future tense: приду (pridu = I will come), not present.
Negated быть (byt) takes the genitive: не будет ответа (ne budet atveta = there will be no answer), ответ (atvet) shifting to ответа.
In a passive, the doer goes in the instrumental: починен моим отцом (pachinen maim attsom = fixed by my father).
благодаря (blagadarya = thanks to) takes the dative, not the genitive: благодаря тебе (... tebe = thanks to you).
с, со (s, sa = off a surface) takes the genitive: стол (stol) becomes со стола (sa stala = off the table).
согласно (saglasna = according to) takes the dative: согласно плану (... planu = according to the plan).
в отличие от (v atlichie at = unlike) takes the genitive: в отличие от брата (... at brata = unlike the brother).
если (esli = if) marks a real condition; don't confuse it with ли (li = whether) for indirect questions, as in придёт ли он (pridyot li on = whether he'll come).
над (nad = above) takes the instrumental: над диваном (nad divanam = above the couch).
без (bez = without) always takes the genitive, so ты (ty = you) becomes тебя (tebya = you).
For location, под (pad = under) takes the instrumental, so стол (stol = table) becomes столом (stalom = table).
скучать по (skuchat pa = to miss) takes the dative, so дом (dom = home) becomes дому (domu = home).
перед (pered = before) takes the instrumental, so сон (son = sleep) becomes сном (snom = sleep).
через (cherez = through) always takes the accusative: через парк (cherez park = through the park).
For location, за (za = behind) takes the instrumental, so дерево (dereva = tree) becomes деревом (derevam = tree).
For moving about a place, по (pa = around) takes the dative: по парку (pa parku = around the park).
у (u = by) means right beside something and takes the genitive: у окна (u akna = by the window).
через (cherez = in) plus a time span means after that time: через час (cherez chas = in an hour).
в течение (v techenie = during) takes the genitive, so день (den = day) becomes дня (dnya = day).
In друг другу (drug drugu = each other) only the second word declines, dative here after помогают (pamagayut = help).
Numbers 2 to 4 force genitive singular on the noun: три года (tri goda = three years).
In reported speech the tense does not shift back: знают (znayut = know) stays present after past сказали (skazali = said).
попрощавшись (paprashchavshis = having said goodbye) is a perfective gerund: the action finishes before the main verb.
из-под (iz-pod = from under) is a single preposition taking the genitive: из-под кровати (iz-pod kravati = from under the bed).
For a range, с (s = from) and до (do = until) both take the genitive: с девяти до пяти (s devyati do pyati = from nine to five).
After ordering or wishing, чтобы (shtoby = that) takes a past-tense verb: чтобы я убрал (shtoby ya ubral = that I clean up).
Some borrowed words like метро (metro = metro) never change form, staying метро (metro) in every case.
The verb ответить (atvetit = answer) needs на (na = to) plus accusative: ответил на сообщение (atvetil na saabshchenie = answered the message).
To place an event in a week, use на (na = on), not в (v): на прошлой неделе (na proshlay nedele = last week), prepositional case.
говоря (gavarya = while talking) is an imperfective gerund: it happens at the same time as ходила (khadila = was walking).
